new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..03673694cae
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/backup/configure-hard-deletion-protection.md
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+---
+title: Configure Hard Deletion Protection in Microsoft Entra (preview)
+description: Learn how to protect supported Microsoft Entra objects from permanent deletion during the first seven days after they're soft deleted.
+author: tazkiaafra
+ms.author: tazkiaafra
+ms.date: 10/12/2026
+ms.service: entra-id
+ms.topic: how-to
+ms.custom: msecd-doc-authoring-1026
+ai-usage: ai-generated
+
+#customer intent: As an identity administrator, I want to protect critical directory objects from immediate permanent deletion so that I have time to restore them after an accidental or unwanted deletion.
+---
+
+# Configure Hard Deletion Protection in Microsoft Entra (preview)
+
+Hard Deletion Protection helps protect critical Microsoft Entra objects from immediate permanent deletion. When you enable protection for an object, the object can still be soft deleted and restored. However, it can't be permanently deleted during the first seven days after it's soft deleted.
+
+Identity administrators can use this article to enable Hard Deletion Protection and view protected objects. To complete the task, you need the **Microsoft Entra Backup Administrator** role and an existing supported object.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Hard Deletion Protection is in preview.
+>
+> Protection is permanent. After you enable Hard Deletion Protection for an object, you can't remove or undo the protection.
+>
+> If you enable protection unintentionally, soft delete the object and wait seven days before you permanently delete it.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An active Microsoft Entra user with the **Microsoft Entra Backup Administrator** role.
+- No additional license is required for the currently supported object types.
+
+Hard Deletion Protection supports:
+
+- Users (on-premises synchronized users aren't supported).
+- Cloud-only groups.
+- Applications.
+- Service principals.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> Microsoft Entra Agent ID objects are supported through their underlying user, application, and service principal object types.
+
+## Understand deletion and restoration behavior
+
+Hard Deletion Protection doesn't prevent soft deletion. It gives you time to investigate and restore an object before permanent deletion is allowed.
+
+- The seven-day protection window starts at the time the object is soft deleted.
+- Attempts to permanently delete the object during the seven-day window are blocked.
+- After the seven-day window ends, the object can be permanently deleted.
+- If you restore the object, Hard Deletion Protection remains enabled.
+- If the restored object is soft deleted again, a new seven-day protection window starts.
+- Enabling Hard Deletion Protection is recorded in the Microsoft Entra audit logs.
+
+When a selected set includes a protected object, the permanent-deletion action is blocked.
+
+<!-- TODO: Replace this paragraph with the final customer-facing blocked-deletion message and add a screenshot when the UX text is finalized. -->
+
+## Enable Hard Deletion Protection
+
+In the Microsoft Entra admin center, you can protect up to 20 objects of one object type in each operation. Objects that already have protection enabled aren't available for selection.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a **Microsoft Entra Backup Administrator**.
+
+1. Browse to **Backup and recovery** > **Hard deletion protection**.
+
+   :::image type="content" source="media/configure-hard-deletion-protection/hard-deletion-protection-page.png#lightbox" alt-text="Screenshot of the Hard deletion protection page with the Add protection button and permanent-protection warning.":::
+
+1. Select **Add protection**.
+
+1. Select one supported object type.
+
+1. Search for and select up to 20 objects of that type.
+
+   :::image type="content" source="media/configure-hard-deletion-protection/select-hard-deletion-protection-objects.png#lightbox" alt-text="Screenshot of the Select objects pane with Users selected, an Add control for object IDs, and the permanent-protection warning.":::
+
+1. Review the permanent-protection warning, and then select **Save**.
+
+1. Review the protected-object counts on the **Hard deletion protection** page. To view protected objects of a specific type, select the corresponding link.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [Soft deletion in Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery](soft-deletion.md)
+- [Recover objects using Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery](recover-objects.md)
+- [Supported objects and recoverable properties in Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery](scope-supported-objects-limitations.md)

englishSummary.headline: Hard Deletion Protection is now documented
englishSummary.summary: The documentation describes protecting supported Microsoft Entra objects from permanent deletion for seven days after soft deletion. It covers prerequisites, supported object types, behavior, audit logging, and setup steps.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators need the Microsoft Entra Backup Administrator role. Protection is permanent, supports up to 20 objects per type per operation, and blocks permanent deletion during the seven-day window.

 #### To configure federation using the Microsoft Graph API
 
-You can use the Microsoft Graph API [samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation](/graph/api/resources/samlorwsfedexternaldomainfederation?view=graph-rest-beta&preserve-view=true) resource type to set up federation with an identity provider that supports either the SAML or WS-Fed protocol.
+Use the Microsoft Graph v1.0 [samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation](/graph/api/resources/samlorwsfedexternaldomainfederation?view=graph-rest-1.0&preserve-view=true) resource to retrieve or create federation configurations. The examples in this section use SAML. To configure a WS-Fed IdP, use the partner's WS-Fed settings and set `preferredAuthenticationProtocol` to `wsFed`.
+
+For delegated access, sign in as at least an [External Identity Provider Administrator](~/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#external-identity-provider-administrator). The access token must have the permissions required for the operation:
+
+| Operation | Microsoft Graph permission |
+| --- | --- |
+| List or retrieve federation configurations. | `Domain.Read.All` |
+| Create a federation configuration. | `IdentityProvider.ReadWrite.All` |
+| Delete a federation configuration. | `Domain.ReadWrite.All` or `IdentityProvider.ReadWrite.All` |
+
+Replace `{token}` with an access token for Microsoft Graph. The sample responses are illustrative and shortened for readability. IDs and configuration values differ in your tenant, and the certificate placeholder isn't a usable certificate.
+
+##### List SAML/WS-Fed IdP federations
+
+Use the following request to [list the SAML/WS-Fed federation configurations](/graph/api/samlorwsfedexternaldomainfederation-list?view=graph-rest-1.0&preserve-view=true) in your tenant:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/federationConfigurations/graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+```
+
+A successful request returns `200 OK` and a collection in `value`:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Type: application/json
+
+{
+  "value": [
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation",
+      "id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
+      "displayName": "Contoso SAML IdP",
+      "issuerUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/saml",
+      "passiveSignInUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/sso/saml",
+      "metadataExchangeUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/metadata",
+      "preferredAuthenticationProtocol": "saml",
+      "signingCertificate": "<Base64-encoded-signing-certificate>",
+      "domains": [
+        {
+          "id": "contoso.com"
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+If the response includes `@odata.nextLink`, request that URL to retrieve the next page. Continue until no next link is returned. For more information, see [Paging Microsoft Graph data](/graph/paging).
+
+##### Find a federation by domain
+
+Use a `domains/any` filter to [find the federation configuration for a specific domain](/graph/api/samlorwsfedexternaldomainfederation-get?view=graph-rest-1.0&preserve-view=true). The following request filters for `contoso.com`.
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/federationConfigurations/graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation?$filter=domains/any(x:x/id%20eq%20'contoso.com')
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+```
+
+The response is still a collection, even when only one federation matches:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Type: application/json
+
+{
+  "value": [
+    {
+      "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation",
+      "id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
+      "displayName": "Contoso SAML IdP",
+      "issuerUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/saml",
+      "passiveSignInUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/sso/saml",
+      "metadataExchangeUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/metadata",
+      "preferredAuthenticationProtocol": "saml",
+      "signingCertificate": "<Base64-encoded-signing-certificate>",
+      "domains": [
+        {
+          "id": "contoso.com"
+        }
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+If no federation matches the domain, `value` is an empty array.
+
+##### Get a federation by ID
+
+To retrieve one federation configuration, use its `id` from a list or domain-filter response:
+
+```http
+GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/federationConfigurations/graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation/11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
+Authorization: Bearer {token}
+```
+
+The response contains a single federation object rather than a `value` collection:
+
+```http
+HTTP/1.1 200 OK
+Content-Type: application/json
+
+{
+  "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation",
+  "id": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
+  "displayName": "Contoso SAML IdP",
+  "issuerUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/saml",
+  "passiveSignInUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/sso/saml",

+```http

+  "metadataExchangeUri": "https://idp.contoso.com/metadata",
+  "preferredAuthenticationProtocol": "saml",
+  "signingCertificate": "<Base64-encoded-signing-certificate>",

+| --- | --- |
+| `displayName` | `Contoso SAML IdP`, a name that helps you identify the provider. |
+| `issuerUri` | `https://idp.contoso.com/saml`, the issuer URI that identifies the partner's IdP. |
+| `passiveSignInUri` | `https://idp.contoso.com/sso/saml`, the HTTPS endpoint for browser-based sign-in. |
+| `metadataExchangeUri` | `https://idp.contoso.com/metadata`, the IdP metadata URL. |
+| `preferredAuthenticationProtocol` | `saml` for a SAML IdP. |

+    issuerUri = "https://idp.contoso.com/saml"

+    -Method POST `
+    -Uri "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/directory/federationConfigurations/microsoft.graph.samlOrWsFedExternalDomainFederation" `
+    -Body $body `
+    -ContentType "application/json"

+```

messageCenterItems.title: Action required: Prepare users who can’t use passkeys for SMS and voice retirement
messageCenterItems.summary: Prepare users relying solely on Microsoft-provided SMS/voice MFA for sign-ins that don’t support passkeys by February 1, 2027 (non-admins) and July 1, 2027 (admins/external). Register compatible alternatives or configure customer-managed telephony to avoid sign-in blocks during phased retirement.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

You’re receiving this message because we detected sign-ins in your tenant involving users who have only SMS and/or voice registered and use sessions that don’t support passkeys.

When Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication is retired, these users may be blocked from completing MFA in those sessions unless they register a compatible alternative method or your organization configures customer-managed telephony.

Rollout schedule

User populationSign-in retirement rollout beginsComplete preparation
Users other than Global Administrators and external usersFebruary 1, 2027Before the applicable rollout reaches your tenant
Global Administrators and external usersJuly 1, 2027Before this separate rollout reaches your tenant

These are phased rollout start dates, not a single cutoff for every organization. Affected users can be blocked when the applicable rollout reaches your tenant.

Important

Microsoft can’t provide each tenant with the specific date the retirement behavior will reach it. Prepare your organization before February 1, 2027, even if the rollout reaches your tenant later. Don’t wait for users to encounter a blocked sign-in before registering an alternative method or configuring customer-managed telephony. The separate rollout for Global Administrators and external users begins July 1, 2027, as shown above.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users who have only SMS and/or voice registered and sign in through browser or device sessions that don’t support passkeys.
  • Detection of these sign-ins doesn’t mean every user or every sign-in in your tenant is affected by this compatibility issue. A user might be able to use passkeys in one environment but still need an alternative method for another.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID sign-in experiences on browser, operating system, or device combinations that don’t support passkeys. Examples can include embedded browser experiences, unsupported browser and operating system combinations, native apps without a supported authentication broker, and environments with platform-specific limitations. Review the passkey compatibility matrix for current support and known limitations.
  • Access to applications and services through those sign-in experiences.

What will happen

When the applicable retirement rollout reaches your tenant:

  • Microsoft-provided SMS and voice will no longer be available to complete MFA.
  • Users with no other available MFA method won’t be able to complete passkey registration in a session that doesn’t support passkeys.
  • Without a compatible alternative method or configured customer-managed telephony, these users will be blocked from signing in through that session and will need administrator assistance.

Registering a passkey on another browser or device doesn’t make the original session support passkeys. Users who continue using that session still need a compatible authentication method.

Action required and recommendations

  • Identify affected users and sign-in environments. Use the tenant list provided with this message to identify users detected in potentially affected sign-ins. For each user, confirm that SMS and/or voice are their only registered MFA methods, then review the browsers, devices, native apps, and embedded sign-in experiences they use. Compare those environments with the Passkey (FIDO2) authentication matrix with Microsoft Entra ID. Include every sign-in environment users need for work; testing only their primary browser can miss another required experience.
  • Register a compatible alternative method. Before retirement reaches your tenant, have affected users register a method that works in their required sign-in environments, such as: 
    • Microsoft Authenticator push notifications 
    • Passwordless phone sign-in with Microsoft Authenticator
    • Time-based one-time passwords (TOTP), such as verification codes from Microsoft Authenticator

Confirm that the selected method is supported in the affected session, enabled for the user, and permitted by applicable Conditional Access policies and authentication strengths. Installing Microsoft Authenticator alone isn’t enough; users must complete the relevant registration and setup.

  • Configure customer-managed telephony if SMS or voice is still required. If affected users must continue using SMS or voice, plan a supported Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication deployment. When available for your tenant, configure the provider for the affected population. Test the provider with the same browsers, devices, applications, and policies those users rely on before the retirement rollout reaches your tenant.
  • Test and communicate. Test the selected alternative method or customer-managed telephony provider using the same browser and device combinations affected users rely on. Verify that users can complete MFA and access the applications they need under your existing policies. Tell users which method to register, how to set it up, and when to complete registration. Notify your helpdesk about the changes and the support path for users who can’t complete sign-in.

Learn more

  • SMS and voice retirement and migration guidance
  • Passkey compatibility with Microsoft Entra ID
  • Passwordless sign-in with Microsoft Authenticator
  • Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication

Compliance considerations

Choose alternative authentication methods that meet your organization’s security and compliance requirements and work in the affected sign-in environments. If you require SMS or voice, review the customer-managed provider’s coverage, terms, privacy, and compliance capabilities before deployment.
